newsitem.title: EU: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - EUROPEAN SINGLE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - EUROPEAN SINGLE MARKET.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
Setting up the legal and legislative framework for a single European market is one thing, putting it into practice is quite another.
Yesterday, the European Commission sent warning shots across the bows of two members states, France and Spain, for failing to open their borders fully to other European insurers.
Both countries have two months to respond to the Commission's comments, described as reasoned opinions, otherwise they may find themselves before the European Court of Justice.

In the case of Spain, the Commission believes there are excessive controls on insurance agents and brokers. It is also concerned about barriers to those wishing to provide insurance services temporarily in Spain.
The complaint against France is that it is not complying with the third non-life and the third life insurance directives which came into force in 1994.
The Commission believes current procedures in France run contrary to these two directives and hamper the introduction of new insurance products.
In a separate development involving insurance yesterday, European authorities showed that they are prepared to act over breaches of the law by fining France Telecom 30 million francs.
Europe's competition court ruled that the national phone company had in 1995 made improper use of its monopoly position to keep a contract with insurer Axa.
Sedgwick's joint venture deal announced yesterday with Italy's Nikols Brichetto makes even more sense when considered in the light of these developments.
Far easier to get into new countries -- including Spain -- with a local partner than setting up from scratch, even though Sedgwick's move is in theory taking place in a single European market.
